stress_implied: At the default earnings and discount rate, this price implies {growth} earnings growth in year one, fading to {terminal} in year {years}.
stress_book: This price is {multiple} times tangible book. A premium over book requires future earnings above the cost of equity.
history_meaning: The historical replay follows 30 companies from 2015 and revalues them annually over ten years. A discount can close as prices rise, earnings weaken or discount rates increase.
stress_title: Rough estimate: what if the assumptions change
stress_owner_note: These are not three forecasts, but a rough estimate under changed assumptions: the business is worth 80%, initial growth drops 3 points and the required return rises 1 point. Left is per-share value; right is margin of safety against the reference price.
stress_bank_note: These are not three forecasts, but a rough estimate for a financial: earnings worth 80%, required return 1 point higher, tangible book unchanged. Left is per-share value; right is margin of safety against the reference price.
eps_desc: The default is the latest per-share earnings the snapshot has. A fiscal-year figure is marked beside the label.
cash_cross_desc: Trial using the median after-capex cash of the latest three years on the same assumptions. A check, not a replacement for the intrinsic value above.
rdcf_growth_desc: The EPS growth rate you expect. Green means it sits below the actual ten-year annualised EPS growth; red means above.
dcf_growth_in_the_next_desc: The growth stage defaults to 10 years. Initial growth is based on historical earnings growth, subject to a cap, and moves toward the second-stage rate. You can enter a rate when comparable history is unavailable.
rdcf_freecashflow_growth_tips_title_neg: Your expected growth rate may be achievable
book_desc: Default Book Value is the tangible book value, which may underestimate or overestimate the real value
rdcf_growth_tips_neg: Expected 10-Year EPS without NRI Growth rate < Actual Historical 10-Year EPS without NRI Growth Rate
rate_live_note: The risk-free rate is the local 10-year government yield for the cash-flow currency, rounded up, plus 6 percentage points. Hong Kong dollar cash flows use the US 10-year as a proxy.
rate_bundled_note: The discount rate uses a previously recorded 10-year government bond yield. You can adjust it.
rate_cached_note: The discount rate uses the most recently available 10-year government bond yield.
discount_rate_desc: Round the 10-year government bond yield for the cash-flow currency up, then add 6 percentage points. HKD uses the US Treasury yield as a proxy. If a benchmark is unavailable, the discount rate is 8%. You can adjust it to your required return.
discount_currency_note: The default discount rate uses the 10-year government bond yield for the cash-flow currency.
stock_search_missing: No covered stocks match. Try another query or enter an exchange and ticker.
stock_search_unavailable: Stock catalog unavailable. You can enter an exchange and ticker.
rdcf_freecashflow_growth_tips_neg: Expected ten-year annualised FCF per share growth <= actual ten-year annualised FCF per share growth
price_edit_here: Edit the reference price beside the company name.
compare_lead: Compare up to five stocks, ordered by margin of safety.
compare_step_add: Type a symbol above, then press Enter or Add.
compare_step_second: Add two or more stocks to compare their margins of safety.
compare_one: Add one more stock to compare margins of safety.
compare_note: The table uses each stock’s default assumptions. You can adjust the inputs on its stock page.
compare_bad: Enter an exchange and ticker, such as SHSE:601398.
compare_dup: The selected stocks are already in the comparison.
total_freecashflow_desc: Defaults to the latest free cash flow per share the sources can supply. Earnings and free cash flow stay separate; neither overwrites the other.
business_predictability_desc: The share of reported years with positive earnings. It helps describe earnings consistency.
rdcf_freecashflow_growth_tips_title_pos: Your expected growth rate may be unreachable
rdcf_growth_tips_title_neg: Your expected growth rate may be achievable
name: Name
chart_fit_note: Historical fit: correlation r = {correlation} for the displayed fiscal years.
fair_value_desc: The main figure is the base-case value per share under the current model. The endpoints show values under different assumptions. Use this as a valuation estimate, not a price target.
rdcf_freecashflow_growth_tips_pos: Expected ten-year annualised FCF per share growth > actual ten-year annualised FCF per share growth
rdcf_implied_desc: The annualised first-stage growth that would make the intrinsic value equal the current price, under the same assumptions. It is not the adopted growth used to compute the intrinsic value, and it is not the historical rate.
rdcf_growth_tips_title_pos: Your expected growth rate may be unreachable
dcf_terminal_desc: The second stage lasts 10 years by default. Continuing value covers the years after that. Both use a default growth rate of 4%, capped at two percentage points below the discount rate.
rdcf_growth_tips_pos: Expected 10-Year EPS without NRI Growth rate > Actual Historical 10-Year EPS without NRI Growth Rate
symbol_format_hint: Format: EXCHANGE:CODE, e.g. SHSE:601398 or NYSE:KO
no_records_yet: No records yet. Use "Record this valuation" to save one.
record_measure_note: Returns and risk follow the record series; with shares they use the position method (flows included), otherwise prices only.
margin_of_safety_desc: How far the price sits below the intrinsic value, as a share of it. Negative means the price is above it.
sensitivity_hint: Discount rate and growth each move two points around the current assumption; the centre cell is the current case.
sensitivity_note: tint = margin of safety against the price
wacc_desc: Cost of equity = risk-free + beta × equity premium + size premium, rounded to a whole percent. There is no debt and no tax here, so this is not WACC.
model_help: Ordinary companies discount per-share earnings, or free cash flow that belongs to shareholders. Banks, insurers and brokers use residual income: the return on book fades to the discount rate.
classification_columns: Limited financial data makes the model choice uncertain.
scenario_note: Scenarios vary growth and discount assumptions
pin_source: Choose a data source for this stock
multiple_check_hint: Apply a target multiple to the per-share base to see the price the market would pay.
multiple_ref_note: The last row is fixed at {multiple}×, i.e. a {rate}% required return: what it is worth once earnings stop growing. Not the intrinsic value.
growth_adopted_note: Historical annualised growth was {historical}%{window}. Forecast growth starts at {adopted}% and moves toward the second-stage rate.
growth_capped_note: Historical annualised growth was {historical}%{window}. Initial growth is capped at {cap}%. The forecast starts at {adopted}% and moves toward the second-stage rate.
growth_missing_note: Historical growth is unavailable. You can enter an earnings growth assumption.
growth_refused_note: Comparable earnings history is insufficient. You can enter an earnings growth assumption.
stage_horizon_note: Both stages cover {years} years. The years after that are capitalized at the second-stage rate.
stage_rate_note: Second-stage growth is not below the discount rate, so later cash flows do not shrink in present value. The years after the two stages are not capitalized; the horizon stays finite.
tbv_double_count_note: Tangible book and earnings are two views of the same assets. Adding book into the intrinsic value counts those assets twice.
reverse_unavailable: Implied growth has no solution when the per-share base is not positive.
basis_unavailable: Per-share data is unavailable for this measure.
reverse_no_solution: No growth rate in range makes the intrinsic value match this price.
reverse_not_started: Start a trial to see the implied growth.
reverse_missing_inputs: Enter a valid reference price and assumptions to infer growth.
stage_cap_note: Stage two and the continuing value both use effective growth of {effective}%. A different discount rate can also change that growth rate.
fcf_basis_fcff: Valuing equity from firm cash flow requires net debt. You can use earnings per share when net debt is unavailable.
fcf_basis_ocf: Operating cash flow and cash available to shareholders are measured differently for banks and insurers. Use residual income for these firms.
residual_income_note: Financial institutions use residual income. In the base case, return on book gradually moves toward the discount rate. The range also shows what happens if the current return persists.
fcf_basis_invest: This measure uses operating cash flow less investing outflows, which include acquisitions and financial investments. Check the filing and distinguish these outflows from capital expenditure when estimating cash available to shareholders.
fcf_basis_equity: Free cash flow is operating cash flow minus capital spending, divided by shares.
fcf_basis_none: Capital expenditure is unavailable in the financial statements. The estimate uses earnings per share.
chart_empty: No historical data is available for this metric.
own_note: from the loaded quote and per-share bases
own_hint: For reference only; none of these change the intrinsic value.
click_row_hint: click a row to switch the chart below
converted_note: Results are converted to {currency} (≈); inputs stay in native {native}
about_lead: Open a stock to see its published valuation and margin of safety. Then try your own assumptions.
about_sources_body: Eastmoney supplies most quotes and financials for mainland China and Hong Kong. US financials mainly come from SEC EDGAR. Published valuations use the financial data and government bond yields recorded for each release.
about_license_body: ValueProbe’s code is open source under the MIT licence. Each data source sets its own terms.
about_sources_timing: The release date, financial period and quote date are shown separately. The margin of safety uses the displayed quote. Enter your own price to see how the margin changes.
about_feedback_body: If a quote, financial figure or valuation looks wrong, include the ticker, the date shown on the page and a source we can check.
home_lead: Search a company or ticker to see fair value, the growth implied by the price, and the margin of safety.
continue_where: Pick up where you left off
sum_lead: The price and the per-share bases.
sum_open_dcf: Value it on the DCF model →
name_as_reported: Company names come from the original data source
watchlist_hint: stored on this device, for coming back to what you follow
watchlist_empty: No watchlist yet — open a stock and tap the star at the top right.
watchlist_step_find: Type a symbol in the header and open its valuation.
watchlist_step_star: Select the star next to the company name to add it.
watchlist_one: Add one more stock to compare valuations side by side.
watch_nothing: No importable symbols in that file
footer_tagline: valueprobe · a local-first, open-source intrinsic value calculator
footer_note: Research use only, not investment advice.
peer_compare_hint: Current P/E and P/BV of listed peers, and the price their median implies.
peer_compare_note: cross-check only, click a name to open it
peer_implied: The median peer P/E implies {price}, {gap} versus the DCF intrinsic value; the bases differ.
peer_unavailable: Reference prices for peers are unavailable
skip_OPERATION_NOT_SUPPORTED: this source does not provide the requested data
skip_RATE_LIMITED: too many requests, try again shortly
skip_RESOLUTION_FAILED: no data found for this stock
discount_hkd_proxy_note: The Hong Kong 10-year benchmark is empty, so the default discount rate uses the US 10-year Treasury as a proxy.
discount_fallback_note: The local 10-year government bond yield is unavailable. The discount rate is 8%, and you can adjust it to your required return.
